private.name: Walden Robotics
private.rationale: Same sector (Robotics & Manufacturing), same stage (Seed), post-money $1.1B

data.narrative:
Westmeg is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $11M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of eight private companies and one public peer (277810.KQ) in the robotics and manufacturing sector. Given the early stage and limited publicly comparable data, peer-median methodology could not be reliably applied—only one same-stage comparable was identified, falling short of the three-datapoint minimum required for statistical robustness.

Stage-progression methodology is applicable and forms the sole quantitative anchor for valuation. Using total capital raised ($11M) as a value proxy and applying a typical Seed-to-next-stage multiplier of 2.5x yields an implied valuation of $28M. This reflects the progression economics observed across the sector, absent company-specific operational or market data that would warrant adjustment.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $23M (low) to $32M (high), centered on a $28M median. The low and high bounds reflect ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression result, consistent with modeling uncertainty at Seed stage. Key limitations include the sparse peer set, lack of meaningful revenue or growth-rate comparables, and reliance on a single methodological pillar. Resolution of these gaps—particularly through tightening the comparable set or obtaining operating metrics—would materially strengthen conviction in this range.
